newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar seen lacking direction, top-heavy in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Dollar seen lacking direction, top-heavy in Asia.

text.p: The dollar is expected to be mostly directionless during Asian trading time on Wednesday amid a lack of fresh incentives, and with gains unlikely as the topside grows increasingly heavy, dealers said.
While dealers said some dollar rises against the yen were possible, they expected gains to be forestalled by exporter sales at highs, with offers emerging anywhere from 122 yen up.

"A key point for today is whether the dollar breaks above 122 yen, with rises to 122.30 yen possible should it manage to do this. From 122.30 yen there is a chance of stop-loss buying, but exporters will also be eager to sell," one dealer said.

He said he expected overseas fund operators, particularly from the United States to join exporters in placing offers, but for dips to be contained near 121.65/70 yen, an important technical support point.
The dollar's moves against the mark were also expected to be limited with slight mark gains against the yen suppressing dollar gains against the German currency.

The mark could take aim at 71.50 yen after testing the downside Tuesday and finding it solid at 71.30 yen. But dealers said that overnight sterling gains against the mark were likely to keep mark rises limited as well.
